newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: ANOTHER COMES FORWARD OVER BONDI KILLING
A second man has come forward to assist police investigating the bashing death of an English tourist at Bondi in Sydney's east more than a week ago.
Last week a 22-year old man went to a police station with a lawyer, was questioned about the death of Brian Hagland, and left.
Meantime, Mr Hagland's body has been released after a second post mortem examination and his girlfriend, Connie Casey, is arranging to return to England for his funeral.
OPPOSITION FINDS HARRADINE MOVE TROUBLING
The Federal Opposition is unconvinced by the Government's statement that it has no plans to end Medicare-funded abortions, in a deal with Independent Senator Brian Harradine.
The Tasmanian Senator has also asked the Government to stop financial assistance to family planning clinics, and the Government needs his vote to get key legislation passed.
Deputy Opposition Leader, Gareth Evans, says there's evidence the Government is already moving to appease Senator Harradine.
Mr Evans says it's a deeply troubling development in Australian politics if such trade-offs come to be made.
DALAI LAMA HOPES FOR MEETING WITH HOWARD
Tibet's exiled spiritual leader, the Dalai Lama, says there would be no problem if Prime Minister, John Howard, refuses to meet him.
Speaking in Melbourne, the Dalai Lama says he hopes for a meeting with Mr Howard, but doesn't want to create any embarrassment if it doesn't take place.
He says he's in Australia mainly for spiritual purposes, and if the Government finds a meeting with him too inconvenient, that's alright.
HMAS MELBOURNE HOME FROM GULF
Australia has no plans to send another ship to the Persian Gulf, following the return to Sydney today of the HMAS Melbourne.
The ship spent five months in the region helping to enforce UN economic sanctions against Iraq.
Defence Industry Science and Personnel Minister, Bronwyn Bishop, says the Prime Minister indicated Australia supported the United States military action against Iraq.
But she says Australia has made no further commitments.
HMAS Melbourne was the fifth Australian ship to take part in the campaign.
LOGGERS MAY BLOCKADE NSW PARLIAMENT
Unionists are threatening a truck bockade of the New South Wales Parliament if a proposal to stop logging in 70 per cent of the state proceeds.
The CFMEU and state opposition say restrictions of that size would kill the timber industry.
They're demanding the Lands and Water Conservation Minister, Kim Yeadon, deliver on promises to protect the industry.
But, with State Cabinet to consider various options this week, Premier Bob Carr says specualtion on the Government's position is premature.
MORE UNIVERSITY PLACES NOT LESS: VANSTONE
Federal Employment Minister Amanda Vanstone says the Government has told universities to make savings in the post-graduate area, not in undergraduates.
Senate Opposition parties are unhappy with Government plans to let universities sell a quarter of places at full fee.
They say this will lead to a U.S.-style system where the wealthy can buy an education but the poor and smart are excluded.
But Ms Vanstone says there'll be six-thousand more
Government-funded undergraduate places at universities next year and more again the following year.
NCA COMPLAINTS UNDERSTATED
The Australian Law Reform Commission has called for an independent body to investigate complaints of corruption against the National Crime Authority and the Federal Police.
President, Alan Rose, has told a Parliamentary Committee on the NCA there are more complaints against it than official figures show.
He says that's because there's no internal process to bring complaints to the NCA's attention.
Mr Rose says the NCA's approach is to deny responsibility and refer difficult cases to the AFP or State police force.
He wants to see an Integrity and Investigations Commission set up to handle complaints against the NCA and AFP.
